title: Windmill
prompt: A labelled scale teaching adaptation of the page 34 windmill combines its post-mill orientation lesson with its exposed geared grindstone train. Wind starts an external bench blower so the four sails and wind-shaft turn. Face wind rotates the mill body around its post to align the sails with the airflow. Feed grain places a small specimen at the grindstone gap. See-through exposes the brake wheel, wallower, vertical shaft, great spur wheel, stone-driving pinions and grindstones. Keep the blower external to the mill and identify the feed fixture as a teaching aid. Do not add a generator, turbine pitch computer or another unsupported drive train.
blurb: A scale teaching adaptation combines a turning post mill and geared grindstones, with an external bench blower and grain feed aid.
truthNotes: Combines the post-mill inset and exposed drivetrain on printed page 34.
Rectangular cloth lattice sails. Jib and spring-sail variants remain separate.
48:16 and 40:12 are illustrative model tooth counts, giving a 10:1 runner-to-sail speed ratio.
Blower and grain feed fixture are teaching aids. Feed grain replaces the specimen after a completed pass.
Grain enters the runner eye and then the physical gap above the fixed bedstone.
2016 page image inspected. Source audit records direct 1998 support. 1988 inaccessible and unverified. No edition-union claim.
